title: A voter can apply their full SKY weight to up to five proposals at once, so approving one does not withdraw support from another
content:
A.1.10.2.6.3 states that "voters can apply their **full** SKY vote-weight to up to 5 different proposals simultaneously (as defined by the `max_yays` limit in the contract), **rather than splitting their tokens between them**."

This is what makes the surrounding system workable. If support were divisible, the instruction to keep weight on the hat (for security) and the ability to back a new proposal (for progress) would be in direct conflict, and every holder would have to choose between defending the status quo and voting for change.

Non-rivalrous approval removes the trade-off up to five slots: a holder can hold the line on the hat and simultaneously endorse its successor with the same tokens. Weight only actually shifts when a voter *removes* their approval from the hat, making disarmament a deliberate act rather than a side effect of participating.

The cap at five is the necessary limit. Unlimited slots would let one holder support every live proposal, which would make their weight informationally worthless — approving everything says nothing about preference and would inflate every threshold equally. A small cap forces some discrimination while preserving the overlap that matters.

Read together with the hat-as-threshold rule, the effective question at each vote is not "do you support this?" but "do you support this *more* than you want to keep defending the incumbent?" — a comparative judgment that only becomes binding when a voter chooses to release their existing approval.
description: A.1.10.2.6.3 makes approval non-rivalrous up to the max_yays limit of 5, letting a holder back a new proposal while continuing to defend the hat.
